what_its_for: Lemborexant is a sleep medicine used to treat adults who have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep (a condition called insomnia). It works by blocking signals in your brain that keep you awake, helping you fall asleep more easily and sleep through the night.
how_to_take: Take lemborexant by mouth as a tablet. Swallow the tablet whole. Take it only when you are ready to go to bed and you have at least 7 hours before you need to wake up. Do NOT take it with or right after a high-fat or heavy meal, as this may slow down how fast it works. Only take it when you can devote a full night to sleep.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 5 mg taken once per night, right before bedtime. Your doctor may increase your dose to 10 mg per night if the lower dose is not working well enough for you. Never take more than 10 mg in one night. Only take one dose per night — do not take a second dose the same night.
missed_dose: If you forget to take your dose at bedtime, skip the missed dose entirely. Do NOT take it in the middle of the night or close to the time you need to wake up. Never double up by taking two doses at once. Just take your next regular dose the following night at bedtime.
storage: Store lemborexant at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in a dry place, away from moisture, heat, and direct light. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Store it out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking lemborexant — it can make you dangerously sleepy. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be fully alert the morning after taking this medicine until you know how it affects you. Avoid taking other sleep medicines, sedatives, or anti-anxiety medicines unless your doctor approves. Avoid taking it with a heavy or high-fat meal right before bedtime, as this may delay its effect.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience any of the following: sleepwalking, sleep-driving, eating while asleep, or doing other activities while not fully awake; unusual or confusing thoughts, hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there); memory loss; feelings of depression or thoughts of harming yourself; worsening anxiety; or if your sleep problems do not improve after 7 to 10 days. Also tell your doctor if you feel very drowsy or unsteady the next day after taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Lemborexant starts working within 30 minutes of taking it, which is why you should only take it right before you get into bed. Some people notice improvement in their sleep right away, while others may need a few nights. If your sleep does not improve within 7 to 10 days, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and over): You may be more sensitive to this medicine and more likely to feel drowsy or dizzy the next day. Your doctor may keep you on the lower 5 mg dose. Be extra careful to avoid falls. Liver problems: If you have moderate liver problems, your doctor will limit your dose to 5 mg. This medicine should NOT be used if you have severe liver disease. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not known if this medicine is safe during pregnancy or if it passes into breast milk. Narcolepsy: Do NOT take this medicine if you have narcolepsy (a condition that causes sudden uncontrollable sleep attacks).
